newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch say EU pig export ban a panic reaction.
newsitem.headline: Dutch say EU pig export ban a panic reaction.

text.p: A recommendation to ban live pig exports from most Dutch districts on Wednesday following an outbreak of swine fever was totally unexpected and smacked of a panic reaction, the Dutch goverment said.

"I have the impression that people have acted out of panic in deciding on these measures," Farm Minister Jozias van Aartsen told Dutch NOS television news. "We have done everything that we were obliged to do, indeed we have done much more."

The ban, expected to be formally imposed by the European Commission in the next few days, was backed by the EU's Standing Veterinary Committee on Wednesday, a Commission official said. It will affect 98 percent of Dutch piggeries, the NOS said.
The Netherlands produced pigs and pork products worth some 5.1 billion guilders in 1996 of which about 60 percent was exported, the Dutch Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said earlier on Wednesday.
Swine fever, last detected in the Netherlands in 1992, is highly contagious, although it is not harmful to humans.
The Dutch government had hoped a quarantine and slaughter policy would be sufficient to contain the disease.
The authorities decided to slaughter all pigs at 26 farms in the area immediately surrounding the first case discovered last week. An estimated 30,000 are expected to be killed.
In addition, they have sealed off a wider area covering some 600 square kilometres, within which the transport of all manure and livestock, excluding poultry, has been banned.
"We must even in this very bad situation...continue to count our blessings," Van Aartsen said.

"(The ban) will be effective only until February 19. I have asked for an EU inspection team...and on the basis of this inspection the Veterinary Committee will decide next week if the measures can be revised."
"So, at first sight, that is still favourable," he said.
Last week, Poland closed its borders to all imports of Dutch pigs, pork and pork products.
The United States said on Tuesday it was banning imports of pork products from the Netherlands because of the swine fever.
